title: Violin lessons and odd jobs at Perkins's shop
summary: Perkins agrees to teach him violin for 75 cents a week; he describes Perkins as a brass band teacher who repaired and rented instruments and taught white and colored pupils.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: So this friend, him and Mr. Dave Perkins, they were good friends. My dad had come from out the Irish Channel.

And so he talked to Mr. Dave and so he told me that Mr. Perkins didn't want to teach no violin. He wasn't bothered by teaching, you know, because he was actually a brass band teacher. Yeah. So he kind of talked a minute and he said, well, okay, I'll send him over. And I was going to school and I had a little job. Like most boys had a job going to school and like yard boy, you know, cleaning up. And I didn't pay but 75 cents a week.
So, yeah, and the lesson, Dave Perkins was charging me 75 cents. Yeah. That just took all my little change there, you know. Yeah. I think I started violin in about, I believe, about two years or so.

Oh, yeah. She was, I mean, he didn't actually play the violin, but he understand the fundamental of it. And he, like in teaching all the instruments, he knew music well, you know. In fact, and I used to have a little job, I used to pick up a little change from him. Like around this time here, he would be getting those instruments fixed up because he rented instruments with the guys, you see.
That would be about countable time.

Yeah, right around now. And he would clean them up and maybe sign them up. And he'd do a few little repairs like putting corks in the valves and things. I mean, the water valves, you know. And I picked up those change like that. Did he have many pupils? Who? Dave Perkins had a lot of pupils. Oh, yes, yes. He taught white and colored, yeah. Yes.
He was a very light fellow, wasn't he?
Very light. He played in brass band. He played sousie bone. Sometimes he played trombone and maybe baritone. Yeah.
I believe Baby Dodd studied under him for a time.

Well, that was one time. I probably, I know a lot of musicians were responsible and got their training for them. Yeah. Maybe they didn't stay long, but if they didn't get their training, they'd come down there and borrow instruments, you know. Yeah.
